messages:
maya: Heads up — during the 03:20 reclaim window in us-west-2 we saw ~4x failed streaming cutovers. Clients observed token gaps and a burst of requeues, ~30s tail-latency spikes. Logs show connection timeouts between runtime and pod-proxy.
sam: I saw that. Root cause looks like egress network flapping on a subset of nodes. Streaming proxy retries hit an idempotency edge (duplicate KV tokens getting lost).
igor: paging ops. impact: some long-lived websocket sessions dropped, retries spawned duplicate sessions and pushed customers over token limits.
lina: timeline? which pools were draining?
maya: timeline: 03:18 network errors start, 03:20 cloud preemptible drain starts, 03:23 most cutovers have failed. Affected pool: mixed-pool-usw2-spot-3 (50% spot, 50% reserved). Last successful handoff ~03:19.
ryan: is this the token-stitch v1 path we still use? I thought v2 was opt-in.
sam: yes v1. It assumes sub-second egress reliability. When egress jitter >5s we lose sequence continuity.
lina: immediate mitigation suggestions?
maya: options: rollback traffic off spot-heavy subpool to reserved-only, or increase graceful drain timeout from 10s -> 45s for that pool in us-west-2.
igor: can clients be nudged to longer backoff and mark sessions resumable for ~1m? That buys time without changing infra.
sam: server-side changes are safer short-term. My proposal: (A) extend drain grace to 45s for the affected pool, (B) enable fallback routing to regional standby pool when handoff ack not received, (C) add explicit handoff ack before cutover.
ryan: also short-term: runtime should not mark token transferred until explicit ACK. And requeue should include seq_id + idempotency key so receivers can detect dupes.
maya: quick proto for handoff API: 

```
POST /v1/handoff
Headers: X-Seq: 12345, X-Idempotency: <uuid>
Body: { "kv_range": "0-1024" }
Response 200: { "ack": true }
```

If no ack -> hold transfer and proxy traffic to standby.
lina: add observability: handoff_ack_rate, handoff_latency_ms, cutover_failure_count. Dashboards and an alert when ack_rate < 95% in 5m.
igor: ops question — can we shift traffic to on-demand (reserved) in region for next 2 hours? Need a safe ramp.
maya: yes. plan: +10% reserved shift every 5m for 30m until healthy.
ryan: cost hit but OK short-term to avoid customer 5xx.
sam: medium-term follow-ups: redesign token streaming to tolerate egress jitter: multiplex over mTLS with keepalive, seq ack, and write-ahead log to object store for last-resort replay. Also add a lightweight lease refresh API to let standby pick up without full cutover.
maya: I'll file follow-up ticket and postmortem. Quick TODOs in order: (1) temp-grace=45s for mixed-pool-usw2-spot-3 (2) enable standby-route fallback for handoff failures (3) create dashboard widgets and alert (4) bump client backoff to 5s -> 15s for streaming reconnects.
deploy-bot: maya triggered rollback: shifted 20% traffic to reserved-subpool-197 and applied +10% reserved ramp plan. CI checks green, rollout started.
lina: thanks. monitor handoff_ack_rate and cutover_failure_count closely. Post updates in this thread.
maya: will update every 5m with metric deltas. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
